annotation.title_clean: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and productivity growth in Kuwait's private sector: Enterprise perspectives and evidence
annotation.title_en: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and productivity growth in Kuwait's private sector: Enterprise perspectives and evidence
annotation.summary_en: ILO report based on 2025 interviews with Kuwaiti private-sector firms on AI adoption and productivity. Finds adoption concentrated in administrative, analytic and customer-facing uses, driven by cost efficiency, with a two-speed gap between large firms and SMEs. Scaling is constrained by data readiness, governance, skills and weak productivity measurement.
key_provisions_or_claims: About 93% of interviewed firms cite cost reduction and faster execution as a key motivation for AI adoption.
Use cases cluster in administrative automation, analytical decision support and customer-facing applications.
A two-speed trajectory separates large, digitally mature firms from SMEs.
Scaling AI depends on data maturity, governance, workforce preparedness and credible measurement.
Findings are indicative of participating firms, not statistically representative.
